name: Pale Olive Green
lede: Pale Olive Green is a light, yellowish green, the color of young olive leaves and some copper minerals.

sections.title: A mineral description
sections.body:
The name is descriptive, a pale form of [[olive-green]] [3]. It appears in the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 [3].

The one book passage we hold uses the words for a mineral. The *Pigment Compendium* says libethenite, a copper phosphate hydroxide, occurs as pale olive green to dark green crystals [1]. It was described by Breithaupt in 1823 and named for its type locality, Lubietová, called Libethen in German [1]. It is a comparatively rare secondary copper mineral found where copper ore has weathered [1]. Greens near this one include [[pistachio]] and [[light-green]] [3].

The swatch on this page is #B1D27B, the screen value we hold for it, which is an approximation and not a measured pigment [3]. Like any pale color it sits between its hue and [[white]], and because the name is a description and not a tradition, other lists may place it a little differently [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Pale Olive Green is rare in our archive: 4 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.02 percent, as photographed [2]. It is rarer than 82 percent of the named colors [2].
